findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the MySQL endpoint a public IP so it is reachable from outside the VPC. Combined with a well-known 'admin' master user, no TLS enforcement and unencrypted storage, this substantially widens the attack surface of the catalog database.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume, snapshots and backups, leaving stored data in cleartext at the storage layer.

Nothing enforces TLS for client connections (the attached parameter group does not set require_secure_transport) and the PHP client uses mysqli_connect without SSL options, so credentials and query data can traverse the network unencrypted to a publicly accessible endpoint.

The master password is passed via var.password and is written into Terraform state (and into EC2 user_data) rather than being sourced from a managed secret store such as Secrets Manager; the variable is not declared sensitive in this configuration.
The master user is 'admin', a well-known default name, which eases credential-guessing/brute-force against an internet-reachable MySQL endpoint.
The mysql8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and omits require_secure_transport = 1, so the database will accept unencrypted client connections.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user_data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF in the PHP app, and is also stored in cleartext in Terraform state, leaking database admin credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. An SSRF in the user-input-handling PHP application would allow retrieval of both the user_data (containing the DB password) and the instance profile credentials for a role holding s3:*/ec2:*/rds:*.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the volume storing the cleartext dbinfo.inc credentials file may be unencrypted at rest depending on AMI/account defaults.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached via instance profile to the internet-facing web server. Theft of the instance credentials through SSRF or RCE would yield near-total control of S3 data, EC2 and RDS in the account, including privilege-escalation paths through EC2 actions.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data-exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.

Ingress on TCP/3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than being scoped to the application instance's security group, so any workload anywhere in the VPC can reach the database directly, defeating network segmentation.
The database endpoint is exported as an unmarked Terraform output; together with publicly_accessible = true this advertises a reachable database host to anyone able to read state or CI logs.
